falsifiable_hypothesis: The existing shrinker already defines PRIOR=0.125 as its fixed conservative floor. Reusing its complement 1-PRIOR=0.875 creates a single shared margin for the two orientation-specific gain guards instead of unrelated constants: the B deployed gain cannot fall below +0.875 when aggregate gain signal is present, and the A auxiliary negative raw gain cannot fall below -0.875. This tests a coherent prior-derived guardrail without any per-fold or per-target routing.
B_rule: Reproduce asymmetric_prior_extended_A_gain signal detection and fallback exactly. The aggregate B gain signal is still detected from the conservative [1,3] bounded vector and its jackknife variance. If global reliability is positive, deploy the raw gain clipped to [1-PRIOR,3]=[0.875,3]. If global reliability is zero, preserve the frozen unanimous-sign fallback.
A_rule: Reproduce asymmetric_prior_extended_A_gain fitting-only A-side bounded-jackknife reliability, global positive-part gate, r_A^3 base confirmation, and two-of-three halfway / three-of-three full confirmation. Use globally fixed raw A bounds [-(1-PRIOR),+0.5]=[-0.875,+0.5]. Apply qA=qA_loo_bagged+0.5*gA_final*theta. The same bounds apply to every target and every outer fold.
margin_rationale: Both changed guards reuse exactly the complement of the already-frozen PRIOR=0.125. This candidate was proposed after development diagnostics and remains repeated adaptive development, not independent validation.
